The assistant turn

In one line: one entry point fills Form A from each typed message, and writes a reply with the next question.

What it is

  • A goal is one move, with its own chat and its own Form A (ADR-0017). A turn is one message: the person types it, and the assistant replies.
  • A visitor chats with no sign-in (PD6b). The first goal of a visitor makes a visitor session, and the API gives the browser a visitor key one time.
  • A handler is one step of a turn. The extractor changes the text into Form A slots. The reply writer plans the reply, and the composer writes its words: see The composer. The router labels each message at the same time as the extractor: see The router. The observer and the advisor become more handlers (PD7a).
  • The token probability is the probability that the model gave to each piece of its answer. The extractor uses it as a gate: a value that the model was not sure of becomes unclear (PD7).

How it fits our project

Part Where
The routes: start a goal, read a goal, send a turn apps/api/src/goals/routes.ts
The goals, the turns and the visitor sessions apps/api/src/goals/store.ts
The entry point: the router and the extractor at the same time apps/api/src/assistant/assistant.ts
The extractor, its prompt and the parsers apps/api/src/assistant/handlers/extractor/
The gate on the token probabilities, and the message of a turn, for each handler apps/api/src/assistant/handlers/gate.ts, turn-message.ts
The reply writer and its lines apps/api/src/assistant/handlers/reply/
The schemas of the routes and the handlers packages/contract/src/goals.ts
  • The visitor key. The browser keeps it in local storage and sends it in the header X-Visitor-Key. The database keeps only its SHA-256, so a log line or an event with the session id opens no chat. A session ends 30 days after the last visit (PD19). A signed-in person sends the token, and the key too until T-17 moves the goals of the session.
  • The words of the person. The model picks enum values, and it copies the words for the areas, the budget and the move date. Code makes sure that the words are in the turn. Then parseBudget and parseMoveDate read them. They know "20k", "lakh", the Hindi and Marathi number words and month names in Latin and Devanagari, "agle mahine", "ASAP" and the date of today in IST. "zyada nahi" makes a maximum, Marathi endings such as "लाखापर्यंत" and "डिसेंबरमध्ये" count, and two amounts are a range only with a word such as "to" or "se" between them. A day and a month in the past go to next year. Words that a parser cannot read leave the slot empty.
  • The area names. A name of the seed gives its areas, also inside longer words, as "Andheri station". The seed has each name in Devanagari too, and a Marathi ending counts, as "अंधेरीत" or "ठाण्यात". A name of two areas, such as "Andheri", leaves the slot empty, and the reply asks "Andheri West, Andheri East, or both?", one line for each such name. A slug that the model picked counts only if its name is in the turn, or in that area question.
  • The gate. Only DeepSeek gives token probabilities. Below ASSISTANT_MIN_PROBABILITY (0.8), a value becomes unclear. A value that the tokens do not hold also becomes unclear, and the API reports it, as an answer of DeepSeek with no probabilities does. Gemini gives none, so its values have no gate.
  • Conflicts. A new value never replaces an earlier stated value (PD3b). The reply asks which value to keep, and the assistant turn keeps that question. The next answer for that slot wins. Each conflict of a turn gets its question. "doosra wala" or "नया" keeps the new value, and "pehla" or "जुना" keeps the earlier value. An answer that settles nothing gets the question again. The extractor reads only the question of the last reply, not the "Got it" line before it. The event slot_conflict records the slot. A new area adds to the areas, and a new budget bound can fill the other bound.
  • The reply. Code plans it. A conflict comes first, then a name of two areas, then an unclear must-have weight (PD15), then the next empty or unclear slot in ASSISTANT_QUESTION_ORDER. On a core turn, the composer writes its words.
  • The events. The first turn of a goal fires interview_started. Each conflict fires slot_conflict, after the save.

The choice we made

  • The router, the small handlers and the extractor that picks only enum values: PD7a.
  • unclear in each enum, and the gate on token probability: PD7.
  • The visitor key, the scripted reply, the area rules and the gate that fails closed: the spec of T-12 (#189).

Gotchas

  • Put fixed text in the system prompt. The prompt holds the enums, the area list from the database and the number forms. It has no date, so the cache of the vendor applies to each turn.
  • The two turns get the time of clock_timestamp(). now() is the same for the whole transaction, so two inserts in two statements keep the reply after the turn of the person.
  • A 409 means that a different tab changed the goal. The second turn does not replace the form of the first. The person sends the message again.
  • The catalogue loads one time for each database. After a change of the area seed, start the API again.
  • In the tests, use scored() of apps/api/test/goals.test.ts. It gives one token for each character, so a test can make one value unsure.
  • The handler schemas use z.strictObject (assistant.md). A misspelled key then fails at once.
